title: count_snapshots and list_snapshots used different location filters
description: Introduced by the WeatherReport-boi fix: list_snapshots was taught to match both the submitted location string and its canonical coordinate form, but count_snapshots was left on exact equality. Since the route computes has_more as offset + len(rows) < total_count, a query like '45.50000, -122.60' returned 1 row with total_count 0, so has_more and total_count both lied. Found while reading the service layer to build the UI, which consumes total_count for pagination.
acceptance_criteria: count_snapshots and list_snapshots agree for every spelling of the same location; the filter is built in one shared place so the two cannot drift again

title: NWS review MAJOR 1+2: station failover and upstream 4xx error mapping
description: Source: docs/NWS_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW.md MAJOR 1 and MAJOR 2 (on master), the two findings that blocked merge of feature/nws-weather-api. MAJOR 1: fetch_observation() only continues the station loop when details['reason'] == 'http_error', so a station returning a non-JSON body (reason='malformed') or a connection-level failure (reason=<ExceptionName>) aborts the whole request and suppresses the remaining candidates. MAJOR 2: an upstream 4xx that is not exactly problem type '/InvalidPoint' falls through to a bare ProviderError (502, log_traceback=True), so a caller-caused condition is reported as a server fault and writes a full traceback on an unauthenticated endpoint - caller-drivable log volume. Cloud-model work: spans app/errors.py, app/services/nws_provider.py and tests/test_nws.py.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed or connection-level station failure falls through to the next station; timeout/untrusted_url/invalid_url still abort; upstream 404 and /points 400 map to a 4xx client error keyed on request kind not on the problem-type string; expected upstream-HTTP provider errors do not log a traceback; new tests cover each branch
close_reason: Both findings fixed on feature/nws-weather-api. MAJOR 1: added STATION_ABORT_REASONS={timeout,untrusted_url,invalid_url}; the station loop now aborts only on those and falls through on every other failure (HTTP error, malformed/non-object body, connection reset, all-null observation). Exhaustion reports stations_tried + last_failure + last_upstream_status. MAJOR 2: _get_json() takes a request kind (point/stations/observation) and maps upstream status on the kind rather than the problem-type string - point 404 -> 404 nws_point_unavailable (even with a non-JSON body), point 400 -> 400 nws_invalid_point, anything else -> 502; all upstream-HTTP errors carry log_traceback=False via a new AppError(log_traceback=...) kwarg, so an unauthenticated caller can no longer drive traceback volume. Station 404s still read as recoverable failover signals, not client errors. 21 new tests in tests/test_nws_failover_and_errors.py reproduce both of the review's exact repro scenarios; 128 tests pass with outbound HTTP proxied to a dead port.

title: Implement real NWS (api.weather.gov) observation provider behind existing WeatherProvider abstraction
description:
Implement a real National Weather Service (NWS) provider behind the existing WeatherProvider abstraction, plus a coordinate-based observations route. NWS is keyless (User-Agent only), coordinate-based, and US-only.

RESEARCH (live-verified against api.weather.gov on 2026-11-23; use these exact shapes)

Base URL: https://api.weather.gov  (Accept: application/geo+json)
No API key. A descriptive User-Agent is MANDATORY — with an empty UA the Akamai
edge returns an HTML "Access Denied" body (not JSON), so the provider must treat
a non-JSON body as a provider error rather than crashing on .json().

1) Point metadata — GET /points/{lat},{lon}
   properties.observationStations -> "https://api.weather.gov/gridpoints/TOP/32,81/stations"
   properties.forecast            -> ".../gridpoints/TOP/32,81/forecast"
   properties.forecastHourly, gridId ("TOP"), gridX (32), gridY (81), timeZone
   - Coordinate precision is capped at 4 decimals; more decimals return HTTP 301
     "AdjustPointPrecision". Round to 4 decimals BEFORE requesting.
   - Outside US coverage (e.g. 51.5,-0.12) -> HTTP 404, problem+json
     type=.../problems/InvalidPoint, title="Data Unavailable For Requested Point".
   - Non-numeric path -> problem+json with parameterErrors[].
   - Response carries cache-control max-age ~24409s: point metadata is stable and
     worth caching.

2) Station discovery — GET {observationStations}
   Top-level keys: observationStations (list of station URLs), features, pagination.
   features[i].properties.stationIdentifier -> "KMYZ"; .name -> "Marysville Municipal Airport".
   Stations are returned nearest-first. An empty list must be handled.

3) Latest observation — GET /stations/{stationId}/observations/latest
   properties.station        -> "https://api.weather.gov/stations/KTOP"
   properties.timestamp      -> "2026-11-24T02:10:00+00:00"
   properties.textDescription-> "Clear"
   Measurements are objects {unitCode, value, qualityControl}, value may be null:
     temperature       unitCode "wmoUnit:degC"
     windSpeed         unitCode "wmoUnit:km_h-1"
     windDirection     "wmoUnit:degree_(angle)"
     relativeHumidity  "wmoUnit:percent"
     windGust          "wmoUnit:km_h-1"  (observed value None in the live sample)
     barometricPressure "wmoUnit:Pa", visibility "wmoUnit:m", dewpoint "wmoUnit:degC"
   A station can return HTTP 404 or a null-valued observation; fall through to the
   next nearest station.

4) Forecast (optional, must stay distinguishable) — GET {forecast}
   periods[] with isDaytime/temperature/temperatureUnit/shortForecast. This is
   FORECAST data, never to be mixed into an observation payload.

Errors are RFC 7807 problem+json: {correlationId, title, type, status, detail, instance}.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (do not duplicate, do not break)
  app/services/weather_provider.py — WeatherProvider Protocol (name, available,
    fetch_current(location) -> dict), UnconfiguredWeatherProvider, HttpWeatherProvider
    (generic OWM-style, key+base_url), normalize() for OWM payloads, build_provider(config),
    serialize_raw().
  app/services/weather_service.py — fetch_current, save_snapshot, get_snapshot,
    list_snapshots (persists location/observed_at/temperature_c/humidity/
    wind_speed_kph/conditions/provider/raw_response).
  app/routes/weather.py — GET /api/weather/provider, GET /api/weather/current?location=,
    POST+GET /api/weather/snapshots, GET /api/weather/snapshots/<id>.
  app/config.py — Config dataclass, env-only, _env_str/_env_int/_env_bool,
    WEATHER_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED gating, to_flask_mapping().
  app/errors.py — AppError, ValidationError(400), NotFoundError(404),
    ProviderNotConfiguredError, ProviderError(502-ish). Reuse these; add none unless needed.
  app/validation.py — require_mapping, required_string, bounded_limit, etc.
  tests/test_weather.py — already covers the unconfigured provider, OWM normalize,
    and the generic HttpWeatherProvider via _FakeSession/_FakeResponse. 67 tests
    currently pass. DO NOT duplicate or rewrite these.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

A. Coordinate validation (new, reusable)
   - Reject non-numeric, missing, out-of-range lat (<-90/>90) and lon (<-180/>180)
     with ValidationError BEFORE any network call.
   - Round to 4 decimals to avoid the NWS 301 precision redirect.

B. New NwsWeatherProvider in app/services (satisfies the existing WeatherProvider
   Protocol: name="nws", available, fetch_current)
   - available is True WITHOUT any API key (NWS is keyless) — it must not be gated
     behind WEATHER_API_KEY.
   - Request chain: /points -> observationStations -> /stations/{id}/observations/latest,
     trying nearest stations in order until one yields a usable observation
     (bounded attempts, e.g. 3, so one bad area cannot cause a request storm).
   - Every request: explicit timeout from config, Accept: application/geo+json,
     and the configured User-Agent header.
   - SSRF guard: the observationStations / forecast URLs come from an external
     response and MUST be validated before use — scheme must be https and host
     must be exactly api.weather.gov. Reject anything else with ProviderError.
     Do not blindly follow arbitrary URLs.
   - Cache point metadata per rounded coordinate (in-process, bounded size) so
     repeated lookups for the same point do not re-request /points.

C. Normalization -> a dict containing AT MINIMUM:
     latitude, longitude            (the requested, rounded coordinates)
     station_id                     (e.g. "KTOP")
     observed_at                    (ISO timestamp from properties.timestamp)
     temperature_c and temperature_f
     description                    (properties.textDescription)
     wind_speed_kph and wind_speed_mph
     source                         ("nws" / api.weather.gov)
     data_type                      ("observation" — never "forecast")
   - Missing or null measurements stay None. NEVER substitute a default,
     an average, or an invented number.
   - Conversions: F = C*9/5+32; mph = kph/1.609344. Convert only when the
     unitCode matches the expected unit; if a unitCode is unexpected, do not
     silently mis-convert.
   - Keep the result compatible with weather_service.save_snapshot (it reads
     location/temperature_c/humidity/wind_speed_kph/conditions/provider), so
     snapshots keep working.

D. Route integration in app/routes/weather.py
   - Add a coordinate-based observation endpoint, e.g.
     GET /api/weather/observations?lat=<lat>&lon=<lon>
     returning {"data": {...normalized...}} with 200.
   - Reuse the existing error envelope and the existing _provider() wiring style.
   - Register the new endpoint in the index listing in app/__init__.py.
   - Existing routes and their status codes must not change behaviour.

E. Configuration (env only, no secrets)
   - NWS_USER_AGENT (descriptive, with contact) — required for live calls.
   - NWS_BASE_URL defaulting to https://api.weather.gov.
   - NWS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (reuse/extend the existing timeout convention).
   - Optionally WEATHER_PROVIDER=nws to select the provider in build_provider.
   - Add the new vars to .env.example with placeholders. Commit NO real values.

F. Error handling — distinct, non-crashing outcomes for:
   - request timeout
   - HTTP 4xx/5xx (including the 404 InvalidPoint "outside US coverage" case,
     which should surface as a clear client-facing error, not a 500)
   - malformed / non-JSON body (the HTML Access Denied case)
   - point has zero observation stations
   - all candidate stations return no usable observation

G. Tests in tests/test_nws.py (new file; MOCKED, no network)
   Mock HTTP via an injected fake session in the same style as the existing
   _FakeSession/_FakeResponse in tests/test_weather.py. Cover:
     valid coordinates; invalid coordinates (non-numeric + out of range);
     successful point lookup; station discovery; observation normalization;
     Celsius->Fahrenheit; wind kph->mph; missing/null observation fields stay None;
     timeout; HTTP error; malformed/non-JSON response; zero stations available;
     SSRF guard rejecting a non-api.weather.gov observationStations URL;
     point-metadata caching (second call issues no second /points request).
   The default suite MUST NOT touch the network.

H. One live smoke test, clearly separated
   - Marked @pytest.mark.live (registered in pytest.ini markers) and skipped
     unless an env flag such as NWS_LIVE_TESTS=1 is set.
   - Uses a valid US coordinate pair (e.g. 39.7456,-97.0892).
   - Must be excluded from the default run (e.g. addopts -m "not live").

I. Green suite
   - The full default suite passes with no network access and no new failures.
   - The 67 pre-existing tests still pass.

CONSTRAINTS
   - Work only in the assigned git worktree on branch feature/nws-weather-api.
   - master must not be touched; do not commit, merge, push, or open a PR.
   - No new runtime dependency beyond `requests`, which is already in requirements.txt.
   - No pip install, no system packages, no sudo.
   - Do not add other weather providers or any geocoding service.
   - Do not overwrite unrelated files.
   - No credentials or real User-Agent contact details committed to the repo.

title: NWS MINOR 8: test gaps at the station step and unit branches
description: Review MINOR 8. Timeout and malformed-body failures were injected only at POINT_URL, so the station abort/retry branch was untested (addressed by WeatherReport-gxo). Still untested: the degF temperature branch, the m_s-1 wind branch, and the two malformed-structure guards in get_point and _stations.

close_reason: Done, with one correction to the issue's premise: the degF temperature branch and the m_s-1 wind branch are NOT still untested - WeatherReport-x3l covered both while fixing the double-rounding bug (tests/test_nws_review_minors.py parametrizes 8 degF and 6 m_s-1 values plus the gust and dewpoint paths). Added beyond the criteria: individual junk entries inside a well-formed features list are skipped rather than fatal (12 parametrized shapes, including a non-matching stationIdentifier, an over-long one and a non-string one) yielding nws_no_stations, and a good feature mixed in among junk is still used. 24 new tests; full suite 255 passed.

title: NWS MINOR 6: no cumulative deadline across the request chain
description: Review MINOR 6. One API call makes up to five sequential upstream requests, each with its own timeout (default 10s) and no shared budget, so slow-but-under-limit responses can occupy a worker ~50s. Per-attempt bounding is correct; worker-time bounding is absent.
acceptance_criteria: A total deadline bounds the whole chain; exceeding it raises the timeout error without starting another upstream request; per-request timeout is the smaller of the remaining budget and the configured timeout
close_reason: Fixed. fetch_observation() now fixes a single deadline (monotonic() + total budget) before the first request and threads it through get_point/_stations/_get_json. _get_json computes remaining = deadline - monotonic() and issues the request with min(remaining, per-request timeout), so a request is never given more time than the chain has left nor more than NWS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. When the budget is gone it raises BEFORE issuing another request: ProviderError reason=timeout, scope=total_budget, 504 weather_provider_timeout, log_traceback=False. reason=timeout is already in STATION_ABORT_REASONS, so exhaustion aborts the station loop instead of being mistaken for a per-station failure - verified explicitly. Budget default is TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER (3) x the per-request timeout, overridable via NWS_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (0/unset/non-numeric derives it; a bad value warns and degrades rather than raising, consistent with WeatherReport-8sz). A cached /points hit spends no budget. 14 new tests in tests/test_nws_budget_and_guards.py driven by an injected fake monotonic clock, so they are deterministic and add no wall-clock time; they assert the exact per-request timeout sequence [10,8,5,2]. Docs gained a 'Timeouts and the chain budget' section. Full suite 255 passed with outbound HTTP proxied to a dead port.

title: NWS MINOR 4: bad NWS_BASE_URL crashes application startup
description: Review MINOR 4. NwsWeatherProvider.__init__ runs the configured base URL through ensure_nws_url and create_app builds the provider unconditionally, so NWS_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 makes create_app() raise ProviderError at import/startup. Contradicts app/config.py's contract that bad values fall back to safe defaults so the app always boots, and makes the knob unusable for a local stub. Fix in build_nws_provider: fall back to the default with a warning; keep the hard ensure_nws_url check for externally supplied URLs.
acceptance_criteria: create_app() boots with a hostile NWS_BASE_URL and logs a warning; provider uses the default base; externally supplied URLs are still hard-rejected
close_reason: Fixed on feature/nws-weather-api. build_nws_provider() now trust-checks the CONFIGURED base URL itself: ensure_nws_url failure is caught, logged at WARNING with the rejected value and its reason, and DEFAULT_BASE_URL is used instead, so create_app() boots with NWS_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 (and 7 other hostile forms: suffix-match, explicit port, wrong scheme, unparseable, userinfo). Same leniency applied to non-numeric NWS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS -> 10. The SSRF guard is unchanged: ensure_nws_url and the NwsWeatherProvider constructor still hard-reject untrusted URLs, so URLs arriving from NWS payloads are not affected. Docs updated to state the knob cannot point at a local stub and that session injection is the way to test against a fake backend. 40 new tests in tests/test_nws_config_fallback.py; full suite 168 passed with outbound HTTP proxied to a dead port.

title: Add pytest coverage for /health degraded and error paths
description:
tests/test_app.py::test_health_endpoint_returns_json_ok covers ONLY the happy path of app/routes/health.py (200 + status 'ok'). Three behaviours of the endpoint have zero coverage:

1. Degraded response: when one or more tables from TABLE_NAMES are absent, health() must return HTTP 503 with status 'degraded', database.connected False, and database.missing_tables listing the absent tables sorted.
2. sqlite3.Error branch: when get_connection()/existing_tables() raises sqlite3.Error, health() must still return a well-formed JSON 503 envelope (no traceback, no 500) and log a warning.
3. weather_provider reporting: the available=True / named-provider branch is never exercised; only the 'unconfigured' default is asserted. The 'environment' field is also never asserted.

The entire 'else 503' arm of 'return jsonify(payload), 200 if database_ok else 503' is therefore dead code from the test suite's perspective — a regression that made /health always return 200 would pass CI today. That matters because /health is the liveness/readiness probe: a container orchestrator relies on the 503 to pull a broken instance out of rotation.

Acceptance criteria:
- New tests added to tests/test_app.py ONLY (no new source files, no changes under app/).
- A test asserting 503 + status 'degraded' + correct sorted missing_tables when a required table is dropped.
- A test asserting the sqlite3.Error path returns a JSON 503 envelope rather than raising.
- A test asserting weather_provider.name/available reflect an injected fake provider, and that 'environment' echoes app config ENV.
- No duplication of the existing happy-path or 405 tests.
- Existing application behaviour unchanged (app/ untouched).
- Full suite green: python -m pytest -q passes with no new failures.
- Work performed on branch feature/health-check-tests in an isolated git worktree; master untouched.

title: NWS informational cleanup: stale docstring, cached dict by reference, docs example types
description: Review INFORMATIONAL items. (a) weather_provider.py docstring still promises no outbound request without credentials, but the keyless NWS route always makes them. (b) get_point returns the cached dict by reference, so a caller mutating it corrupts shared state. (c) int(getattr(response,'status_code',200) or 200) fails open - a missing/falsy status reads as 200. (d) docs example renders wind_direction_deg/barometric_pressure_pa/visibility_m as ints though _number casts to float. (e) docs label an example 'a real reading from KTOP' with provenance only in the issue tracker. (f) the SSRF test asserts only the exception type, not details['reason'].
acceptance_criteria: Docstring matches behaviour; cached point is copied on read; a missing status code no longer reads as success; docs example types and provenance corrected; SSRF test asserts the reason
close_reason: Fixed, all six items. (a) weather_provider module docstring rewritten: it no longer claims the app never makes outbound requests without credentials - it now states that the keyless NWS provider DOES call api.weather.gov as soon as WEATHER_PROVIDER=nws selects it, that selection is itself the opt-in, and that ensure_nws_url confines the traffic. (b) get_point copies on read AND on the cache-miss return path, so no caller holds a reference to shared cache state. (c) the 'int(status_code or 200)' fail-open is gone; a status that is missing, non-numeric or outside 100-599 now raises malformed instead of reading as 200 - note a present-but-falsy 0 needed the range check, not just the None check, and the test that proved it uses a VALID payload so it cannot pass for the wrong reason. (d) docs example now renders wind_direction_deg/barometric_pressure_pa/visibility_m as floats and explains that _number() casts unconditionally. (e) the example is labelled illustrative rather than 'a real reading from KTOP'. (f) the SSRF test is parametrized over (url, reason) and asserts details['reason'] so it cannot pass if the guard stops running and the request fails for an unrelated reason. 5 new tests in tests/test_nws_review_minors.py plus the strengthened test_nws.py SSRF case; full suite 217 passed.

title: NWS MINOR 10: snapshot location filter misses the submitted string
description: Review MINOR 10. location is rebuilt as f'{latitude},{longitude}' from rounded floats, so a snapshot POSTed as '45.50000, -122.60' is stored as '45.5,-122.6' while list_snapshots filters on exact string equality - a client listing by the string it submitted gets zero rows.
acceptance_criteria: Listing snapshots by a coordinate string that differs only in formatting returns the stored rows; non-coordinate locations keep exact-match behaviour
close_reason: Fixed on both sides, because fixing one leaves a hole. Added weather_service.canonical_location(), which returns the canonical 'lat,lon' form of a coordinate pair via parse_coordinates or None for free text. (1) save_snapshot now stores the canonical form, so storage cannot fragment into un-joinable groups by spelling. (2) list_snapshots matches the submitted string AND its canonical form (WHERE location IN (?,?) when they differ), covering odd spellings and rows written before this behaviour existed. Non-coordinate locations keep exact case-sensitive matching rather than guessing at place names. Worth recording: my first version canonicalized only the QUERY side and my own tests caught that a canonical query then missed a row stored verbatim - that failure is what prompted the write-side change, and the test was rewritten to assert what the fix actually delivers instead of being relaxed. Known limit, documented: pre-existing non-canonical rows are matched by their own string, not retro-canonicalized, which would need a migration. 36 new tests in tests/test_snapshot_location_filter.py including 9 canonicalization cases, 12 non-coordinate rejections, and pagination through both the IN and exact-match branches. Full suite 291 passed with outbound HTTP proxied to a dead port.

title: NWS MINOR 9: double rounding on non-canonical input units
description: Review MINOR 9. _temperature_c rounds a degF input to 2 decimals and c_to_f rounds again, so 33F round-trips to 33.01F; same pattern for m_s-1 wind. Output can disagree with the upstream reading by 0.01.
acceptance_criteria: A degF input round-trips to the original value; an m_s-1 wind round-trips consistently; conversions round once, at output
close_reason: Fixed. Conversions now round exactly once, at output. _temperature_c/_speed_kph return a _Reading(value, converted) NamedTuple carrying the EXACT canonical-unit value plus whether a unit conversion was applied; normalize_observation reports the paired _f/_mph figure via c_to_f/kph_to_mph fed from reading.value (full precision), so 33 degF now round-trips to exactly 33.0 instead of 33.01. Deliberate refinement over the literal criteria: a value already in canonical units (degC, km_h-1) is passed through UNROUNDED rather than rounded at output, because rounding a passthrough would make our output disagree with upstream for no reason - the existing test asserting wind_speed_kph == 16.09344 caught this and is correct. Only converted values are rounded (_present()). 23 new tests in tests/test_nws_review_minors.py; full suite 217 passed with outbound HTTP proxied to a dead port.

title: NWS MINOR 7: unvalidated forecast URL is cached
description: Review MINOR 7. observationStations is guarded by ensure_nws_url but the adjacent forecast value is stored verbatim in the point cache. Nothing fetches it today, so it is latent, but the guard is non-uniform at the extraction site and the first consumer inherits an SSRF.
acceptance_criteria: forecast is validated at extraction; an untrusted value does not reach the cache; the point lookup does not fail because of this unused field
close_reason: Fixed. Added _optional_nws_url(): same ensure_nws_url trust check, different failure mode - returns None instead of raising. get_point now stores forecast=_optional_nws_url(props.get('forecast')), so an untrusted value never reaches the point cache, while a bad value in this unused field does not fail the observation lookup that does not depend on it. observationStations keeps the hard ensure_nws_url check and still raises untrusted_url, verified by a dedicated test so the two failure modes cannot be confused. 16 new tests in tests/test_nws_review_minors.py covering 7 hostile forecast values through both the cache and the full request path; full suite 217 passed.

title: NWS MINOR 5: usable observation discarded when timestamp is absent
description: Review MINOR 5. _is_usable requires observed_at, which is only set when properties.timestamp is a str, so a payload carrying temperature and textDescription but no timestamp is rejected and the whole request ends as nws_no_observation/502. Conservative but lossy.
acceptance_criteria: An observation with measurements but no timestamp is returned with observed_at null rather than discarded; a payload with neither timestamp nor measurements is still rejected
close_reason: Fixed. _is_usable no longer requires observed_at; it returns True when any of temperature_c/humidity/wind_speed_kph/description is present. A station reporting measurements with no (or a non-string) properties.timestamp is now returned with observed_at null instead of being discarded and collapsing the request into nws_no_observation/502. A payload with no measurements at all is still rejected, which is the condition that actually makes an observation worthless - verified explicitly, including the empty-properties case. Docs note that observed_at is nullable. 5 new tests in tests/test_nws_review_minors.py; full suite 217 passed.
